newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BNDES kicks off Brazil's telecoms sell-off - paper.
newsitem.headline: BNDES kicks off Brazil's telecoms sell-off - paper.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) last week began to work on the bidding process to hire advisors on the sale of Telesp and Embratel, expected for early 1998, a local financial newspaper said.
Telesp is an operator of the federally-owned Telebras system serving Sao Paulo state, while Embratel is Telebras' long-distance unit.
Jose Pio Borges, BNDES vice-president and Privatization chief, told Gazeta Mercantil newspaper that the results of the bidding process would be announced this year.

Borges said that winning consortia will only work on the evaluation and the sale of the companies. The privatization model will be designed first by the United Nations' International Telecommunications Union, according to the newspaper.

Gazeta said 26 of Telebras' operators will be grouped in four areas. Only Telesp will be sold separately, it said. Telebras' 27 operators have an estimated base price of 5.0 billion reais, Gazeta added.
